root_cause.text: In the Xe DRM GuC submission suspend path, an idle-queue optimization incorrectly skipped the normal suspend/schedule-toggle flow for non-parallel exec queues, preventing the required GuC context switch and TLB flush for userptr VMAs in LR/preempt-fence VM mode.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says “The idle-skip optimization bypasses GuC suspend, so the GPU may not perform the context switch that flushes TLB entries for invalidated userptr VMAs… Restore unconditional schedule toggling on suspend so the context-switch TLB flush is always performed,” and the patch removes `xe_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend()` plus all checks that bypassed suspend/resume handling in `__guc_exec_queue_process_msg_suspend()`, `__guc_exec_queue_process_msg_resume()`, and LR suspend logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the inline xe_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend helper from the header.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the entire static inline helper function xe_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend() from the header, including its kernel-doc comment and its implementation that returned true when an exec queue was both non-parallel and idle.
intent_record.how: This eliminates the public inline predicate for checking whether suspend steps can be skipped for an exec queue. Any callers must now rely on another definition or location for this logic, but the behavior itself is not changed within this hunk because the function is simply removed from the header.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the `EXEC_QUEUE_STATE_IDLE_SKIP_SUSPEND` exec queue state flag definition.
intent_record.what: The macro definition `EXEC_QUEUE_STATE_IDLE_SKIP_SUSPEND` was removed from the exec queue state bitmask definitions.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates that specific state flag from the codebase, so any code that previously referred to this bit will no longer be able to use it; by itself, the hunk only removes the definition and does not add replacement logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused exec queue idle-skip-suspend state helpers.
intent_record.what: The diff removes three static helper functions from the file: exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(), set_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(), and clear_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(). These functions previously read, set, and cleared the EXEC_QUEUE_STATE_IDLE_SKIP_SUSPEND bit in q->guc->state.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this change eliminates the dedicated wrapper functions for manipulating the IDLE_SKIP_SUSPEND state bit. Any remaining code in the file can no longer call these helpers, so the suspend-skip behavior must either be unused or handled elsewhere. The change does not introduce new logic; it only removes this local API surface.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always update the ring tail for non-parallel exec queues in the replay submission path, removing the idle-skip suspend condition.
intent_record.what: The conditional `else if (!exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q))` was simplified to an unconditional `else`, so `xe_lrc_set_ring_tail(lrc, lrc->ring.tail);` now runs for all non-parallel exec queues in this branch.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the ring tail is now updated regardless of `exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q)` for non-parallel queues, changing suspend/idle-skip related behavior so the tail state is always committed in this path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the idle-skip exception so GuC exec queues always follow the suspend wait path when state changes are allowed.
intent_record.what: The local variable `idle_skip_suspend` and its assignment were removed from `__guc_exec_queue_process_msg_suspend()`, and the `if` condition no longer checks `!idle_skip_suspend`; the suspend wait is now entered whenever `guc_exec_queue_allowed_to_change_state(q)`, `!exec_queue_suspended(q)`, and `exec_queue_enabled(q)` are all true.
intent_record.how: This change makes the suspend path run even for queues that previously would have skipped suspend due to the idle-skip condition. As a result, the function will wait for the GuC recovery/state condition more broadly, rather than bypassing suspend handling for that class of exec queues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused suspend-related state handling and delete the local sched_context submission helper.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the conditional call to set_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q) from the suspend-message handler when suspend_pending is set, and completely deletes the static sched_context(struct xe_exec_queue *q) helper function, including its assertions, trace call, ring tail update, and GuC command submission.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the suspend path will no longer mark the exec queue with the idle-skip-suspend state from this branch, and the code no longer provides a direct helper to submit a SCHED_CONTEXT action to GuC from this file. This reduces behavior in the suspend flow and removes a context-scheduling path that was previously available here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify exec queue resume handling by removing idle-skip-suspend-specific logic from the resume message path.
intent_record.what: The diff removes all handling of exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend() from __guc_exec_queue_process_msg_resume(): it deletes the block that reset the skip-suspend flag and updated the LRC ring tail when the queue was disabled, deletes the alternate branch that only cleared the flag and called sched_context() when the queue was already enabled, and also removes the unconditional clear_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q) from the failure path. The remaining logic now only clears the suspended state, marks the queue pending resume, and enables scheduling when the queue is not enabled.
intent_record.how: At runtime, resume processing no longer performs the special idle-skip-suspend recovery actions in this function. That means the ring tail is no longer forcibly restored here, the idle-skip-suspend flag is no longer cleared in these paths, and the resume flow becomes simpler and limited to transitioning the queue back toward scheduling if it is disabled. Any cleanup or tail adjustment previously done here must now happen elsewhere or is no longer needed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify faulting LR job suspend handling by always marking affected queues for resume and removing the idle-skip-based suspend path.
intent_record.what: In the loop over `group->exec_queue_list`, the local variable `idle_skip_suspend` was removed. The code no longer calls `xe_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q)`, no longer conditionally returns `-EAGAIN` based on that flag, no longer increments `XE_GT_STATS_ID_HW_ENGINE_GROUP_SKIP_LR_QUEUE_COUNT`, and no longer accumulates `need_resume` with `!idle_skip_suspend`. Instead, after confirming `xe_vm_in_fault_mode(q->vm)`, it now returns `-EAGAIN` whenever `has_deps` is true, increments only `XE_GT_STATS_ID_HW_ENGINE_GROUP_SUSPEND_LR_QUEUE_COUNT`, unconditionally sets `need_resume = true`, and then suspends the queue.
intent_record.how: This changes suspend handling for faulting LR jobs so that any queue encountered in fault mode is treated as requiring a resume later, regardless of its idle-skip state. It also removes the special-case skip counter and makes dependency presence the sole reason to defer suspension with `-EAGAIN`, which changes when the suspend operation proceeds and how statistics are reported.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown diff already contains the idle-skip safeguard that prevents the vulnerable suspend-path shortcut from applying in the wrong cases. In `__guc_exec_queue_process_msg_suspend()`, the normal suspend/schedule-disable path is now gated by `if (!idle_skip_suspend && guc_exec_queue_allowed_to_change_state(q) && !exec_queue_suspended(q) && exec_queue_enabled(q))`, and when the idle-skip state is active it sets `EXEC_QUEUE_STATE_IDLE_SKIP_SUSPEND` and still marks the queue suspended: `if (idle_skip_suspend) set_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q); set_exec_queue_suspended(q);`. More importantly, on resume the code either restores the ring tail and re-enables scheduling, or explicitly performs the missing GuC context scheduling step via `sched_context(q)` for enabled queues: `} else if (exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q)) { clear_exec_queue_idle_skip_suspend(q); sched_context(q); }`. The helper `sched_context()` also does `xe_lrc_set_ring_tail(lrc, lrc->ring.tail); xe_guc_ct_send(&guc->ct, action, ARRAY_SIZE(action), 0, 0);`, which is the required context switch/schedule action. This indicates the bug-triggering omission is already fixed in this commit, not present.
